why: The arrangement is resolved TWICE, in two languages, on purpose: the server
resolves it for design_read_layout (ruling 3 — the answer is the arrangement
as the panel shows it, not the document), and the client keeps resolving it
locally because the Pages panel renders optimistically, before any round trip
(`resolveRouteOrder` in v2_fe/src/lib/design-layout.ts, `groupedPages` in
v2_fe/src/pages/design/pages-order.ts, mirrored by `resolve_route_order` and
`panel_sections` in backend/plugins/taskflow-design/src/layout_doc.rs).
That duplication is structural, but UNPINNED duplication is not: both rule
sets have already changed once (pages-order.ts records a wrong earlier move
rule and a changed section-drawing rule), and prose naming the other
implementation cannot fail when the two drift apart.
So there is ONE table of cases and TWO readers of it, and a one-sided change
to either rule set turns this file red on that side:
* backend/plugins/taskflow-design/tests/layout_doc.rs (via include_str!)
* v2_fe/src/pages/design/layout-panel-cases.test.ts (via readFileSync)
`doc` is a layout document exactly as the server stores and sends it
(`layout_doc::LayoutDoc`), `manifest` is the project's route list in manifest
order, and `expect` is the panel's answer: the FLOW, the groups with their
pages, the pages no group claims, and the NAME each page is listed under.
Both sides assert all four.
`names` is the fourth rule, and it is the label-or-title COMPOSITE: a page
reads as its `pageLabels` entry where it has one, else as its manifest
title (`layout_doc::page_name` on the server, `pageLabel` in
v2_fe/src/lib/design-layout.ts on the client). It covers EVERY page of the
manifest, not only the labelled ones — a table that named just the labelled
pages would go green the moment a reader stopped applying labels at all,
which is exactly the mutation it exists to catch.
Both readers pass the ROUTE as the page's title, because the harness has no
manifest reader (titles come from the server's `manifest::title_for`, which
has its own tests). So an unlabelled page's expected name is its own route,
and what this table pins is the CHOICE between label and title — not how a
title is derived. A blank label would be a false drift rather than a real
one (the client's `normalizeLayout` DROPS a blank label and the server's
`validate` refuses to store one), so no case carries one.

cases.name: a fresh project lists every page ungrouped, in manifest order
the stored flow orders the pages it names, and every page it does not name is appended in manifest order
a group's pages are listed in flow order, not in the order its own routes array holds
groups keep the document's order, and the ungrouped pages are the complement
a route two groups claim lists under the first of them, and an empty group keeps its section
a hand-edited document naming a page that is gone, and naming one twice, keeps its grouping and drops what it cannot place
a page reads as its label where it has one, and as the manifest title where it does not
